issue.title: Getting-started provider wording test expects obsolete fixed Grok alias pools
issue.description: Proposed by phase sase-1ao.2 note #1 as a clean-base docs provider wording failure; independently reproduced while landing sase-1ao on clean master e922c424e with .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -n 0 tests/test_docs_getting_started_providers.py. tests/test_docs_getting_started_providers.py::test_getting_started_muse_grok_wording_separates_provider_selection asserts that docs/getting_started.md names @small, @medium, @large, and @xlarge exactly, but commit ec25a1a33 (sase-1aa.5.2) intentionally replaced static pool enumerations with a generated-table link. Update the assertion to verify the stable distinction between PATH autodetection and alias routing plus the generated link, without reintroducing manually pinned pool membership. This is separate from closed sase-m3, which removed the overloaded explicit-only wording in August.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: The documentation prose was deliberately changed by ec25a1a33 while the test still asserts the prior exact static string. The node failed in a serial focused run on the clean tree; the text mismatch is deterministic.

evidence.note: Proposed by sase-19x.9 note #5: the getting-started docs assertion remains red on current master after linked Rust extension restore; serial focused run of tests/test_docs_getting_started_providers.py gave that exact obsolete Grok pool wording failure (2 failed/154 passed batch).

sase-1ab land agent: proposed by sase-1ab.2 note #3; reproduced at sase master 7b20f4c1c in the full fast suite (-n 16) and a serial rerun. The node still asserts the old static Grok pool sentence. Not caused by the turn rename.

Independently reproduced during sase-1bf's landing full-suite check escalation (tool run db269817c4f912574f05104c4e0a6782, sase master 965248789b + this tale's 3 fixes): docs/getting_started.md still lacks the asserted static Grok Build pool wording. Unrelated to sase-1bf, not fixed here.
